question: What is the theoretical value of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant (σ) which defines the power emitted per unit area by a black body as a function of its thermodynamic temperature?
solution: The correct answer is __**4**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • **The Stefan-Boltzmann constant**, represented by **σ**, defines the power emitted per unit area by a black body as a function of its thermodynamic temperature. • **Theoretical Value:** The theoretical value of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant is approximately **5.67 × 10⁻⁸ Wm⁻²K⁻⁴**. This is derived from fundamental constants in physics. • The Stefan-Boltzmann constant is used in the **Stefan-Boltzmann Law**, which states that the total energy radiated per unit surface area of a black body is proportional to the fourth power of the black body's absolute temperature. *Hence, option 4 is correct.* • The formula for the Stefan-Boltzmann law is given as: **P = σT⁴**, where **P** is the power emitted per unit area, **σ** is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, and **T** is the absolute temperature of the black body. • The constant arises from combining other physical constants, such as the speed of light (**c**), Planck's constant (**h**), and Boltzmann's constant (**k**). • Other values in the options are incorrect as they deviate significantly from the experimentally determined and theoretically derived value of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant. • ***Hence, the correct answer is 4.*** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • **Derivation of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant:** • **σ** is derived from fundamental constants using the formula: **σ = (2π⁵k⁴)/(15c²h³)**, where **k** is Boltzmann's constant, **c** is the speed of light, and **h** is Planck's constant. • Its value is approximately **5.670374419 × 10⁻⁸ Wm⁻²K⁻⁴**, which is universally accepted. • **Applications of Stefan-Boltzmann Law:** • Used to calculate the **radiative heat transfer** from black bodies. • Helps in determining the luminosity of stars and other celestial bodies. • **Example:** The Sun's radiative power can be estimated using its temperature and surface area. • **Importance in thermodynamics:** • It establishes a relationship between temperature and radiation, which is crucial in studying thermal properties of objects. • It is widely used in astrophysics, climatology, and engineering. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** • **Black Body Radiation:** • A **black body** is an idealized physical body that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation, regardless of frequency or angle of incidence. • The Stefan-Boltzmann law specifically applies to black bodies, making it a cornerstone in thermal radiation studies. • **Experimental Validation:** • The value of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant has been verified through experiments in labs and astronomical observations. • It is consistent with observations of radiative heat transfer and stellar luminosity. e7:T2901,
